To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SIV infection of macaque monkeys can be used to study viral factors that determine the ability of SIV to cause neurological disease and to study host factors that influence the development of AIDS dementia complex.

(1) SIV infection of macaque monkeys can be used to model the progression to AIDS Dementia Complex (ADC); (2) SIV enters the brain very early in infection, before clinical signs appear; (3) the virus replicates in brain cells; (4) SIV infection is accompanied by a strong inflammatory response in the brain; (5) the virus uses CXCR4, CCR5, and/or CXCR6 for entry to the brain and to cause disease

SIV infection in macaques is an excellent model for the study of HIV infection in humans and that the SIV/macque model can be used to identify viral and host factors that affect the development of neurological diseases in humans.

the following: (1) identifying viral factors that are necessary for the development of AIDS dementia; (2) determining the timing of HIV entry into the CNS; and (3) characterizing the immune responses that affect HIV entry into the brain and the development of AIDS-related neurological disease.
